thread:
kim: quick heads-up — noticed p95/p99 token latency spike on tool call validation after last kernel-selector deploy. dashboard shows per-token breakdown: validation time jumps from ~0.6ms -> ~3.2ms on a subset of routes. attaching initial notes.

dev-infra-bot: deploy kim/kernel-selector-v2 -> success 1769998895

sasha: I pulled a flamegraph from a profiling run on the affected instance. validate_structured_output is the hotspot — a lot of time in memcpy and proto parsing. looks correlated with KV cache misses that force context rebuilds.

sasha: snippet:
```
# hotspot summary
validate_structured_output()  58% cpu
parse_proto_field()          22% cpu
kv_cache_lookup_miss()       17% cpu
```

mdev: did the kernel selector change sequence-length bucketing? v2 had a heuristic change for small sequences that might pick a kernel without gather fast-paths.

jules: confirmed — kernel chooser now prefers matmul-kernel-v3 for seq_len <= 64 in many shapes. v3 doesn't include the optimized gather for broadcasted K/V, so we end up doing extra copies and a fallback path that rebuilds KV frames.

kim: can we emit a metric like `kv_cache_rebuild_ms` per-request? current cache_hit_rate hides rebuild tail cost.

sasha: added temporary trace spans and metrics on canary nodes: `kv_rebuild_time_ms` and `validation_ms`. early numbers: kv_rebuild_time median 0.8ms -> 2.5ms on affected flows; validation_ms median 0.6ms -> 3.8ms.

mdev: short-term workaround: bias the batch sampler to group similar seq_len requests together so we avoid cross-shape batches that trigger the v3 path. batcher config: `prefer_bucket=true`, `bucket_tolerance=8`. spinning up a canary.

infra-bot: rollout kim/batch-sampler-bias -> started canary (5%) 1769999005

kim: canary update (10m): p95 token latency down ~18% on route `chat.toolcall.validate`. validation retry metric also fell from 7% -> 2%. good signal but some payloads with many small structured fields still show high validation_ms.

jules: proposed follow-ups: (1) add `kv_rebuild_time_ms` to per-route KPIs in Console and token-level latency breakdown; (2) add unit tests in kernel-selector for gather fast-paths and ensure matmul-v3 has fallback microbenchmarks; (3) evaluate adding a quantized gather kernel for v3 to avoid copies.

kim: I'll file a Jira and put these on the weekly perf sync agenda. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

(quick todo: kim -> create JIRA PERF-2321, sasha -> keep canary traces for 24h, mdev -> promote batch sampler bias if green)
